title: Carbon dioxide enrichment in greenhouses
body: The concentration of CO2 in the atmosphere is very low, between 0.03 and 0.04 per cent, and CO2 is the major limiting factor for photosynthesis. C3 and C4 plants respond differently to CO2. At low light neither group responds to high CO2, but at high light intensities both show an increase in the rate of photosynthesis. C4 plants show saturation at about 360 µL/L of CO2, while C3 plants continue to respond to increased CO2 and saturation is seen only beyond 450 µL/L. Farmers growing tomatoes and bell peppers in greenhouses therefore release extra CO2 into the greenhouse air. Plants grown in this CO2-enriched atmosphere give higher yields, although very high CO2 levels can become damaging over long periods.
